U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 7 Impact of Radiation on Fire Spread § Radiation is the conversion of thermal energy into EM waves § Radiation can both heat and cool fuel § Impact of radiation on heating unburnt fuel is influenced by factors such as o Fire intensity o Smoke, Water Vapor, Ash…etc o Terrain & Structure of Fuel § Radiation transport is one of the more difficult items to model due to high uncertainty in describing fuel structure and absorption by soot Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 8 Impact of Spotting on Fire Spread § Spotting implies the following: o Burning material (tree limbs, paper, etc…) are first lifted up o The material continues to burn (size dependence) during transport and o Lands and possibly starts new fires that can contribute to overall spread § Primary mechanism for fire spread in a lot of situations (especially for high winds) § Description or modeling of spotting is highly uncertain (source, continued burning, and ignition) and handled in a probabilistic manner Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 9 Impact of Environment on Fire Spread § Environment includes the following: o Fuel: moisture, structure, spacing, size, explosive component (chemicals, refineries), retardants o Weather: wind speed and shear, humidity, atmospheric stratification, precipitation, pyrocumulus o Terrain o Building: frame composition, inside material and spacing, rubble o Interacting large-scale fires o Ignition patterns § Each component can have uncertainty in both time and space… § Significantly impacts ability to model fire spread Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 10 Current Models used to Simulation Various Aspects of Nuclear Weapon
